title: Aivu, grandson of Rav
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Sukkah 44b, Aivu and Chizkiyah, the sons of Rav’s daughter, brought a willow branch before Rav. As Hyman explains in his article on Rav, he also identifies the grandson with the Aivu mentioned on the same folio who, in the reading Hyman follows, spoke in the name of R’ Elazar bar Yitzchak.

notes.text: The supplied source has the malformed כרתיה. The consulted Sukkah paragraph reads בני ברתיה, “sons of his daughter,” supporting the bracketed translation rather than a person named Kartiah. Its other Aivu reports Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok, whereas Hyman here writes bar Yitzchak; that discrepancy remains unresolved.

Supplied כרתיה remains beside the earlier consulted Sukkah44b ברתיה, supporting the bracketed daughter rather than a person Kartiah. That prior paragraph has Elazar bar Tzadok against Hyman’s bar Yitzchak; neither the entry Rav nor Dikdukei Soferim was newly inspected. The finite search is not universal manuscript absence. With no new full-title witness for this exact Yitzchak occurrence, its title remains R'. Leading כ is read contextually as in.

Hyman’s printed notice on p. 138 reads בני ברתיה, “sons of his daughter,” where the supplied transcription has כרתיה. Davidson Sukkah 44b likewise identifies the willow bearers as Rav’s daughter’s sons and gives Elazar bar Tzadok in the surrounding Aivu episodes. Dikdukei Soferim records bar Yitzchak for the encounter (pp. 136–137, notes ט and כ) and separately for the named transmission (p. 137, note ש). In his article on Rav, p. 16, Hyman prefers bar Yitzchak for the encounter and identifies that Aivu as Rav’s grandson. The textual variants leave the identification open.
